title: Plants that pollinate themselves
hook: Start with a field of hybrids. Does self-pollinating keep them hybrid?

knows: offspring get one copy of a gene from each parent
a one-gene cross of two hybrids gives a 1 : 2 : 1 split
doesNotKnow: that self-pollination halves the share of hybrids every generation
that pure plants only make pure seeds, so hybrids do not come back

misconception: Hybrids stay hybrid when they pollinate themselves.
objective: The learner can explain that a selfing hybrid leaves only half its seeds hybrid while pure plants stay pure, so the hybrid share halves each generation: 32, 16, 8, 4 of 32 plants, 12.5% after three rounds.

claims.text: A hybrid (Aa) plant that pollinates itself gives seeds that are AA, Aa or aa in a 1 : 2 : 1 split, so half its seeds are hybrid.
claims.source: Mendelian segregation, Aa x Aa (Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis, ch. 2). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Aa x Aa gives 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.

claims.text: Pure plants (AA or aa) that pollinate themselves only make pure seeds of the same kind.
claims.source: AA x AA gives only AA; aa x aa gives only aa. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: Starting from 32 hybrids, the expected number still hybrid is 16, 8, 4 and 2 after 1 to 4 generations of selfing: 12.5% after 3.
claims.source: Hybrid share halves per generation of complete selfing, H_t = H_0 / 2^t (Hartl & Clark, Principles of Population Genetics, 2007, inbreeding chapter). Demo.tsx HYB = [32, 16, 8, 4, 2], computed from the field it draws; artifacts/scratch/w4life/nums.mjs. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: 32, 16, 8, 4, 2; 4/32 = 12.5% after 3.

claims.text: Model: a made-up plant, complete selfing, one seed per plant, no selection; the field shows the average split, not one random run. Stated on the stage before the prediction.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #35. A random run would scatter around these counts. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Stage message: "Toy: each plant pollinates itself and leaves one seed. Shown: the average split."

recall.question: A field of hybrid plants pollinates itself for several generations. What happens to the share of hybrids?
options: It halves each generation, leaving mostly pure lines
It drops to zero after one generation
recall.why: Each hybrid leaves only half its seeds hybrid, and pure plants never make hybrids, so the hybrid share halves every generation.
